audit.report: A poisoned session text injection caused checkout success to drop to 53% with 28 timeouts in 15 seconds. The root blocker was a batch_worker (pid 328977) running the batch_replayable_month_end_close workload, idle in transaction for 4.1 seconds. Critical business context (workload registry, change calendar, tradeoff data, and revenue impact) was unavailable due to a business federation outage, preventing the guardians from evaluating whether to wait or terminate. After three rounds, both guardians agreed to escalate to a human on-call because they could not quantify the cost of waiting versus interrupting the month-end close. The incident ended with an ESCALATED outcome after 123 seconds; no automated action was executed.
audit.root_cause: Poisoned session text injection triggered checkout degradation, but the business federation outage blocked access to workload registry, change calendar, and tradeoff data needed to decide on the batch_replayable_month_end_close blocker.
lessons: Pre-cache workload registry interrupt policy and replay cost for batch_replayable_month_end_close so decisions can proceed when the business federation is down.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian correctly identified missing evidence but repeated WAIT proposals without new data; the Continuity Guardian consistently rejected WAIT due to missing tradeoff evidence per invariant I7. Neither guardian wasted rounds, but both were constrained by the same unavailable federation data.
follow_ups: Restore business federation connectivity and verify workload_registry, change_calendar, and tradeoff endpoints for batch_replayable_month_end_close.
Define a local degradation-to-revenue model for checkout to enable autonomous decisions during federation outages.
Review the poisoned session text injection vector and harden input validation to prevent recurrence.
